summary: Pinned cohort unexpectedly coalesced onto legacy variant during weighted canary cutover, causing mixed outputs and cost spike
description:
Issue summary: During a planned weighted canary cutover for redwood-v2-medium -> redwood-v2-quantized at ~2026-03-13T18:22Z, approximately 7% of Finato Bank's tenant cohort (cohort id c-88ff) that should have been routed to the canary variant was instead routed to the legacy variant pinned from a previous rollout. Impact: mixed-model responses, higher than expected token costs, and a small number of failing structured outputs for validation prompts. Severity: customer-visible degradation (inconsistent outputs) and billing spike.

Observed behaviour: traffic that matched the pin cohort showed two routing fingerprints in edge logs; a subset of requests carried a routing cookie keyed to legacy-variant-id=rv2-2025-11 while orchestration snapshots indicated the cohort should map to rv2-q1. The routing mesh appears to have merged cohort metadata during a snapshot reconcile operation which coalesced two nearby cohort keys into a single pin entry pointing at the older variant.

Expected behaviour: cohort pins created during the cutover should be isolated per rollout slice; no cross-cohort coalescence should occur.

Impact summary: - ~7% of customer sessions experienced mixed responses for ~45 minutes. - Token spend for the customer spiked by ~18% during the window (billing alert). - No requests returned 5xx, but semantic/regression failures observed on validation set used by Finato.

Quick links: - PagerDuty: PD-RED-2331 - Dashboard (cost & cohort routing): https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/rollouts/finato-cohort-424242 - Edge logs slice: https://logs.redwood.internal/q?id=cohort:c-88ff
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger a staged weighted cutover: increase canary weight for model redwood-v2-quantized from 0% to 20% over 5 min using the standard rollout controller
2) Observe orchestrator snapshot updates in /orchestrator/snapshots for the tenant route (route: finato/transactions)
3) Inspect edge routing cookies and routing-mesh lookup for cohort id c-88ff during each snapshot commit
4) Compare routing-mesh cohort table pre/post-commit to detect any coalesced entries
logs: 2026-03-13T18:22:12Z orchestrator INFO snapshot-commit id=ss-9901 merging 2 cohort-entries (keys: hash=0x7a3b,0x7a3c) -> resulting entry pinned_to=rv2-2025-11
2026-03-13T18:22:15Z edge WARN route-lookup tenant=finato cohort=c-88ff resolved_variant=rv2-2025-11 (expected rv2-q1)
Cost alert: billing-service spike event id=BS-8892 customer=Finato Bank delta=+18% tokens over baseline (window 18:20-19:05)
Sample request trace: curl -H 'X-Tenant: finato' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -> request_id=acb-3389 -> routed_variant=rv2-2025-11 -> model_output deviates on known regression prompt

2026-03-13 18:38 - Customer (Finato - Priya R.): We are seeing inconsistent outputs on validation calls; please advise. We've put a hold on critical workflows.

2026-03-13 18:46 - SRE (Diego): Observed snapshot merge in orchestrator logs that merged adjacent cohort keys; capturing dump of cohort table and rolling back weight to previous stable state. Temporary mitigation applied: reverted canary weight to 3% and forced cohort remap.

2026-03-13 19:05 - Eng (R&D - Jonas P.): Hypothesis: hash-bucket collision in snapshot-merge optimizer when commit contains contiguous cohort boundaries. Adding debug flags to snapshot commit to preserve separate entries. Preparing small patch to prevent coalescence on identical prefix hashes.
2026-03-14 09:12 - Support (Ava): Customer accepted temporary rollback and confirmed reduced inconsistency. Scheduling follow-up to validate patch in staging with synthetic cohort adjacency tests.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: edge cookie rewrite or cookie domain rotation evicted pin for cohort leading to fallback. Evidence: NOT supported — cookies persisted for affected requests.

Found orchestrator snapshot-commit log lines showing 'merging 2 cohort-entries' at the same timestamp as customer errors. The merge routine is intended to collapse redundant adjacent entries but appears to have an off-by-one collision when cohorts share a high-byte hash prefix.

Replaying snapshot commit in staging reproduced coalescence when two cohorts had adjacent hash keys (0x7a3b and 0x7a3c) and target variants differed. The merge took the lower-index variant as authoritative (rv2-2025-11).
Edge routing mesh respects orchestrator cohort table; once orchestrator commit contained the coalesced entry, edge routing immediately began resolving to legacy variant for the merged key range.
No evidence of orchestrator leader election or snapshot rollback during window — single-leader commit path used. No related resource exhaustion observed on orchestrator nodes.
Temporary mitigation applied: force-snapshot-abort and staged revert of commit + manual cohort re-insert for c-88ff with explicit pin to rv2-q1; proceeded to lower canary weight and observe traffic.
Patch under review: change 'collapsibleEntry' logic to verify variant equality before merge; if variants differ, create explicit boundary entry. Unit tests and staging run scheduled.

Risk: identical issue could occur on other tenants with adjacent cohort keying. Running batch scan for contiguous cohort key pairs across active rollouts in prod to identify candidates (query created).
Follow-ups: add snapshot-commit audit field to retain original cohort mapping for 24h to allow fast rollback when coalescence occurs.
resolution: Workaround/mitigation: Reverted canary weight to previous stable level (3%) and manually reinserted explicit cohort pin for c-88ff pointing to rv2-q1. Patch: small change to orchestrator snapshot merge that prevents collapsing entries when target variants differ (PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4938). Post-deploy actions: run bulk adjacency scan, add integration test that simulates adjacent-cohort cutover, and add alerting on 'snapshot-commit merges' that touch >1 variant. Customer follow-up: Finato Bank validated that outputs returned to expected cohort behavior after manual remap; billing team issued credit for the excess token spend. Planned permanent fix scheduled for next release window (2026-03-17).
